observations: The supplied raster contains four horizontal access ports, two on the left and two on the right.
The upper and lower guides are mirror images: each access port transitions through a rounded S-bend into a long straight center section, then returns through a rounded S-bend.
The two center sections run parallel with a small constant gap, which identifies the functional coupling region.
The black-device bounding box is approximately 1898 px by 739 px and is calibrated by footprint.json to 120 um by 4 um.
topology_reasoning.operation: Light launched into either input guide couples across the close parallel center sections; the coupling strength is set primarily by the center-section length and inter-guide gap, while bend radius and guide width control routing loss and the access transition.
topology_reasoning.construction: Use only gf.Path/extrude waveguide primitives for two mirrored routed centerlines, assembled in a @gf.cell and written on layer (1, 0).

iterations.change_made: Initial two-path gf.Path model with constant-width coupling guides and smooth cubic S-bends.
Corrected GDS-to-raster Y orientation, assigned the wider guide to the visual upper rail, shifted centerlines, and matched asymmetric left/right port positions.
Replaced cubic bend shape with measured horizontal-tangent S-bend profiles from raster landmarks.
Tested separate guide-specific bend progressions to capture the rasterized access asymmetry.
Corrected the visual-guide profile assignment after skeletonizing the target and retained the best per-side progression.
Used the target skeleton's sharp common centerline turn profile and moved width transitions into the early access bends; stopped at the six-iteration limit.
